note: Shows blocks with a chart per step: each block adds one note, and its own neck puts exactly the notes named so far in play (enable) and rings the one just added (highlight), ending on a tune that uses only those notes and comes back in G from the Key row. The neck shows the frets and the note names, so the text names only the degrees.

exercise.title: Do, Mi, Sol on the neck, one note at a time
exercise.focus: C major in open position · Do → Do Mi → Do Mi Sol → a tune, then in G
exercise.why: Do, Mi and Sol are the three notes of the C chord, so adding them one at a time shows how a tune is built from a chord you can already fret.

sections.text: Only {{1}} is in play on the neck below. Find it on the A string, then on the B string, and hop between the two.
{{3}} joins it, ringed on the neck below. From each {{1}}, find the nearest {{3}} above it. Play the pair, then play it backwards.
{{5}} joins them, ringed on the neck below. Play {{1}} {{3}} {{5}} {{3}} {{1}} from the lowest {{1}}, until you can do it without looking at the neck.

Press Play below to hear a short tune made of only these three notes, and play along with the neck. Once you can hum it before you play it, tap G in the Key row above the neck. The notes change, the pattern doesn't.
